Multiplayer

Build a game with Replay

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Run the engine-free modelChoose the runtime ownerPut gameplay dependencies in WorldConnect GodotAuthor a larger game

Replay organizes gameplay around a World: a typed value containing all mutable simulation state. A frame captures that state at one tick. The runner retains frames and input, restores a prior frame when necessary, and reruns subsequent steps with the revised input. Godot owns input devices, scenes, animation, and effects outside that world. Replay is experimental; consult the support and runner contracts for the configuration you intend to ship.

Run the engine-free model#

Start with Loot, a small Odin executable that changes the winner of a pickup:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_loot/run.sh

The model predicts one inventory transfer, revises the input at tick 1, rebuilds eight ticks, and compares the result with an independent run. The same operation restores the chest, both inventories, entity lifetime, pool metadata, and RNG.

Read the complete model and its timeline lifecycle. A local input revision demonstrates restoration; network authority is established by the network runner and session policy.

Choose the runtime owner#

Need Owner Small reference
Local replayable simulation Timeline Loot
Godot game with direct offline, host, server, client, or observer roles Session Session starter
Invitations, enrollment, rejoin, and elected authority recovery Party and Room Replay Cavecrawl
Deterministic fixed-roster peer rollback Admitted P2P setup and p2p.Runner Duel

Pump the owner you chose. Room drives its Session; a direct Session drives its clock, transport, and runner. Keep live runtime owners at stable addresses and close dependent objects before their borrowed resources.

Put gameplay dependencies in World#

Include every mutable value needed for the next tick: positions, health, inventories, cooldowns, scheduled work, RNG, entity membership, and allocation metadata. Use supported value types and handles. Keep node references, sockets, audio playback, and persistent storage outside the frame.

A step reads the world, typed input, simulation tick, and fixed versioned definitions. Read devices before stepping. Record occurrences during the step to describe gameplay results, such as a pickup or a hit. Presentation uses their Begin, Update, Confirm, and Cancel changes to create, revise, confirm, or remove effects after replay. The frame contract describes transaction boundaries and history limits.

Connect Godot#

The Session starter contains an offline and native host/client game. Edit shared/game/game.odin for rules and scripts/starter.odin for input and presentation. Use its documented role environment variables to start separate local host and client processes.

The checked lifecycle recipes instantiate Session, Party → Room, and P2P setup against the public API. Hello's network scene shows the lower-level runner integration when you need custom orchestration. Follow starting a Replay game for the full choice of owners and imports.

Author a larger game#

The Scrapyard contributor guide follows a shared turret from authored Resources through World, actions, and scene views. Use its workbench to change one feature in isolation. The code guide maps responsibilities to files; the support envelope records the limits of tested configurations.
